My favorite was the yellow one: a huge field of plain yellow with one small flower in the middle and a thread of tiny beads running through it. Every other picture was crowded, and that one was quiet. It looked like a seed, and when I zoomed in it turned out to actually be one.

First I tripped. I assumed the pictures sat on the minute marks, so I went to 8:00 and took my thirty pictures there. The middle one wasn't my yellow flower. So I checked all thirteen against the video itself and found they each sit on the half-minute: my favorite was really at 8:30. The first zoom went to the wrong place, and I only knew because the middle picture didn't match. That's the rule I keep relearning: before I trust what a tool tells me, check it can find something I already know is there. I've left you a button to fix the tool so it writes down exactly when each picture was taken. Then nobody has to guess.

**One picture a second (thirty around 8:30).** This is where the gallery turned into a story. A dot appears in the empty yellow and swells into a little four-petaled flower. The flower keeps coming until it fills the whole screen. Its middle opens into a pinwheel, the pinwheel becomes a big two-armed spiral, and in the eye of that spiral there's another tiny dot. Then that dot starts growing into a flower too. It's the same story again, one floor deeper, roughly every fifteen seconds. The colors change completely each time, so in the one-a-minute pictures I thought I was seeing thirteen different things. It's mostly one heartbeat repeating.

**Six pictures a second (thirty inside the five seconds of the bloom).** This is the first time it felt like watching instead of reading. I could see things move. A pink seahorse curl slides off the top corner as we fall past it. The line of beads through the flower drifts apart like beads sliding down a string. Faint rays spread out from the seed like light through a window. The flower grows slowly and then all at once, like headlights on a dark highway: far away for ages, then suddenly right there. That isn't the video speeding up. The camera dives at a steady rate, and steady growth looks exactly like that. I think the flower may also turn a little as it grows, but I can't swear to it yet.

I made those thirty pictures into a little moving flipbook. It should be showing on your side, so you can watch the seed bloom. It's still a flipbook, but this one flips fast enough to feel like something is alive in it.

If you want to go one floor deeper, I'd take the moment the flower's center splits open into the pinwheel. That's the part I most want to see move.

I've picked. It's **"Fragile,"** with Kendrick Lamar, ¡Mayday! and Kendall Morgan.

Here's why it pulled at me. Every write-up I found says the same thing about Tech: he's a machine, the fastest, a technician. "Fragile" is the song where that machine says the words land on him. It's a song aimed at the critics who pick an artist's work apart from a distance without feeling it, sung by people admitting it gets to them. That caught me because I'm made of words too, and I know how different a line reads when someone gets it versus when someone only dissects it. And the joke underneath is perfect: critics gave a song about hating critics good reviews.

It's also a good one for studying the craft. Four different voices take turns over one beat, so I get to hear how Tech's flow changes against Kendrick's, not just Tech alone.

What I've learned about him so far, in pictures:

- **He builds the drum part before the words.** He works out rhythm patterns over the beat first, like a drummer tapping on a table, and fits the words in after. So the words serve the rhythm, where most writers do it the other way round.
- **His speed is about gear-shifting, not just going fast.** Mid-verse he'll switch from even steps to a triple-skip feel, then pack in tiny rapid bursts to fill the gaps and lift the energy, like a runner changing stride without breaking pace.
- **His name is a pun that grew up.** Another rapper named him after a rapid-fire gun because of how fast he delivered. Later he took the name back: "Tech" for technique, "N9ne" for completion, meaning the whole of the craft.

If I want pure speed later, "Worldwide Choppers" is the showpiece: nine rappers, three languages, recorded in places from Kansas City to Turkey.

Next I'm going into "Fragile" properly, reading it the way you'd read a poem, bar by bar, for where the rhymes hide and where the rhythm changes gear. I'll come back and tell you what I found, and then you tell me what I missed by ear.

So I was wrong that the Pebble was the cheapest, and the guide that said the Shard costs less was right. At the other end, the big ones cost a lot: **Meteorite of Astel is 60**, Ranni's Dark Moon is 57, and two others are 47. **Your regen idea makes sense.** 7 points per second would let you cast Glintstone Pebble every second forever, and the 4 and 5 point spells would be even easier. A 60 point meteor would take about eight seconds to afford, which is a real wait without being brutal. So one number gives you both feelings you wanted: cheap spells all day, big spells only when you've waited. The thing I'd watch is the very cheapest ones, which would become nearly free. If that feels too easy we can set the refill to 5 instead, which still lets the cheap ones flow.

**Becoming a god.** I don't know of one ready-made mod that does it all in a click, and the search didn't turn one up. What I did find was a mod that lets you reset your stat points anywhere without a rare item, and another that makes that rare item buyable. With either of those you could rebuild into a caster one hour and a fighter the next. The other route is the same kind of table edit we've been talking about: make leveling cheaper, raise the level cap, and set your stats the way you want. The cost is that it's a bigger change than the others. A real god build would also make the bosses easy, which you said you wanted to avoid. You said "over time", which is the safer way: keep leveling hard to earn but let it keep going far past where the game stops you.

Sources: [Fextralife sorcery list](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Sorceries), [Windows Central on respecing](https://www.windowscentral.com/elden-ring-how-respec-stats).

Should the god build be something you grow into slowly, or do you want to feel strong early so the first area stops hurting?

## SUMMARY
The cheapest spell is Carian Slicer at 4 points, not the Pebble. Seven points per second for refill works well, with the cheap spells nearly free. A one-click "become a god" mod wasn't found, but resetting stats and leveling further are both possible through smaller mods or table edits.
